key_insight: FracLearn teaches a language model to improve physical design by converting simulated fracture experiences into reusable design principles, then applying them to new architectures.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path to AI copilots for materials and structural design that learn from experiments and transfer hard-won physical knowledge without retraining model weights.
method: Generate candidate architectures for a fracture game and observe simulated responses.
Abstract experience into conditional rules linking reinforcement placement, crack evolution, and load transfer.
Generalize by recombining learned rules on new designs to surpass prior records.
evidence_signal: In campaigns, the model achieved a best composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record, with fracture analyses attributing gains to crack deflection, temporary trapping, and higher residual load capacity.
watch_item: The framework was tested in a deliberately unfamiliar, game-like setting, so transfer to real materials and manufacturing constraints still needs validation.
paper_title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
